Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle as the Sri Lankan players are seen in a huddle on the boundary ropes before striding out to the middle as well. It will be the prolific pairing of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran to open the innings for Afghanistan. It will be the left-arm seam of Dilshan Madushanka to get proceedings going with the ball here.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 242 is the number required for Afghanistan to rack up their third win of the campaign and add to their impressive run in this tournament. Sri Lanka have their task cut out but have the pace attack to challenge the opposition. It looks like a straightforward target but sometimes, scores of around 240-250 provide us with an enticing game. Do join us in a bit for the run chase.

Rashid Khan is down for a chat. He says it is a great achievement for him to play for his country and reach 100 ODI matches. Adds that the wicket is good to bat on but they bowled well. Tells that they assessed the conditions quickly and they wanted to restrict them under 250. Mentions that after the last game, the confidence is high and they just want to play positive cricket. Says that they had a couple of practice sessions and saw that India vs Bangladesh game here and knows that there could be dew under lights. Ends by hoping that they can win this one and make his 100th game a bit more special.

Afghanistan would have taken this score at the toss and the bowlers have backed their skipper's decision to bowl first. On a pitch that looked nice and hard, Fazalhaq Farooqi picked up an early wicket and along with Mujeeb Ur Rahman kept a check on the flow of runs as well. Azmatullah Omarzai then came in and got a big wicket, breaking the 2nd wicket partnership and after that Afghanistan were able to boss the middle overs. The likes of Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi gave nothing away but it was Mujeeb who once again came in and got a couple of big wickets in quick succession. The fielding too was brilliant as the fielders consistently scored direct hits and that brought about a couple of run-outs as well. Naveen-ul-Haq had an off day as he took some pounding in the final ten overs but Farooqi justified his selection to the fullest as he ripped through that lower order and finished with 4 for 34, the second-best bowling figures by an Afghan bowler in a World Cup game.

End of an up-and-down first innings but at the halfway stage, Afghanistan will be more than happy with that effort, restricting Sri Lanka to just 241 runs. Sri Lanka were put into bat by Hashmatullah Shahidi and the change up top didn't work as Dimuth Karunaratne got out early. Two of their three most prolific batters in recent times, Pathum Nissanka and skipper Kusal Mendis put on a steady stand but were found guilty of being content with just the singles on offer. As they looked to shift gears, they just weren't ready and soon Nissanka fell. The skipper then added another stand with Sadeera Samarawickrama but once again they just didn't show enough intent and the settled pair fell in the space of a couple of overs. After that it was left upon Angelo Mathews and the tailenders to muster up some crucial runs and Maheesh Theekshana did just that as he scored a vital 29 and Matthews too scored 23 runs but they have fallen well short of what would have been a par score on this wicket.

Match number 30 of the 2023 World Cup is upon us and it will be Afghanistan taking on Sri Lanka at the MCA Stadium in Pune in what will be a very crucial encounter. Both teams have played five matches thus far, winning 2 and losing 3 but both sides come into this contest on the back of stellar wins. Afghanistan have been knocking on the door for quite a while now and have shown their prowess in the T20 format but after a winless 2019 World Cup campaign, they have now racked up a couple of big wins, none so bigger than their demolition of neighbors and cricket powerhouse Pakistan in the last game. Chasing a score of 280 plus, they lost just a couple of wickets with the top 4 all contributing to the win. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran are a lethal pair and once these two get going, Afghanistan seem to have a pretty easy game but the form of skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi has been a big positive as well. The bowling is well-rounded with the likes of Naveen-ul-Haq, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Rashid Khan providing variety and wicket-taking ability as well but the addition of Noor Ahmad against Pakistan was a masterstroke as he picked up three wickets and all that experience playing in the Pakistan Super League seemed to have paid dividends. Sri Lanka on the other hand had a really tough start to the tournament and were involved in a couple of high-scoring losses and given their injury list, they seemed to have no chance going forward. But a couple of wins, including a rout of England in their previous game has certainly galvanized them. The top order has fired pretty consistently with Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis ​​​​Kusal Perera all playing useful knocks and then the stability provided by Sadeera Samarawickrama and Charith Asalanka gives them that added advantage over their opponents. The bowling has been a concern in general but Dilshan Madushanka and Lahiru Kumara have stepped up at the right time with Maheesh Theekshana doing a fine overall job. Two sides that know each other really well and for both, a win will see them really challenge for that semi-final berth but a loss could all but end their campaign. Which underdog team will make the maximum impact and get that crucial win? We shall find out.
